questions.prompt: How can distraction interfere with performance?
questions.answer: Task-relevant attentional resources may be diverted to unrelated concerns.
Conscious control of a well-practised process may interfere with fluent execution.
questions.feedback: Distinguish a novice's need for instruction.

questions.answer: No; responses depend on the task, context and individual.
Errors may reflect skill gaps, ambiguity, access or other demands rather than pressure alone.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer, formative only; use specific feedback and delayed retest.
scoring.practice: Distinguishes pressure mechanisms, proposes rival explanations and chooses safe task-specific support.
scoring.transfer: Map a new fictional performance problem, including two rival explanations and one task-specific support. Explain when the support might be inappropriate. Set up a low-risk comparison without deliberately inducing anxiety.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; never average away missing or safety-critical evidence. Quizzes cannot certify competence.
